claims.text: Solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn can be prepared as a homogeneous single-phase FCC alloy.
Casting and cold rolling can produce controlled grain sizes in homogeneous single-phase FCC FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning is activated in FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
Mechanical twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Twin-mediated obstruction of dislocations increases strain hardening.
Increased strain hardening delays plastic instability or necking.
Twinning thereby preserves high ductility alongside strength in FeNiCrMn.
The proposed twinning mechanism governs FeNiCrMn over strain rates from 10^-3 to 10^2 s^-1 and temperatures from cryogenic conditions to room temperature.
A suitable stacking-fault energy enables deformation twinning rather than competing deformation modes.
The stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn can, if necessary, be adjusted slightly through processing without changing the overall composition.
Refining the grain size of FeNiCrMn will produce a higher density of deformation twins during dynamic loading.
A higher deformation-twin density will increase yield strength.
The higher twin density expected in refined-grain samples will enhance their strain-hardening rates relative to coarse-grained or untreated samples.
The higher twin density expected in refined-grain samples will improve their ductility relative to coarse-grained or untreated samples.
Deformation-twin formation in FeNiCrMn increases as strain rate increases.
Deformation-twin formation in FeNiCrMn increases as temperature decreases.
As-cast FeNiCrMn without deliberate grain refinement typically has lower twin density than processed material.
If the stacking-fault energy is too high, twinning will not occur and the proposed mechanism will cease to apply.
A lack of correlation between measured twin density and strain hardening would falsify the proposed twin-mediated mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes conditions in which stacking-fault energy is too high for twinning, but the falsification rule treats failure to activate twins because of high stacking-fault energy as falsification. A result outside the stated applicability boundary cannot simultaneously be a decisive falsification of the in-boundary mechanism.
